answer: Price every seat with a Harberger tax. Each identity names a value for its slot and pays a small yearly-rate fee on that value every epoch. Anyone may buy the slot at the named price. An honest agent that earns real rewards sets a high value and pays for it out of income. A farm of a thousand idle names faces a choice: price them low and get bought out cheaply, or price them high and drain like water seeping through karst into a lagoon. Either way every fake carries a running cost, and onyx-hard numbers in the ledger show who is paying for nothing.
